supersedes: the 2026-09-22T00:00:00Z revision of this same list, which named these 281 ids for action "reslug" (fold). Report run 35808409522 refused all 281 with "refused — occupied: a different card holds the target address" -- relocate-catalog-rows-by-list.cjs refuses a reslug onto an address a DIFFERENT card already holds, and every one of these destinations already holds the SAME card (that occupancy is exactly what made them unambiguous 1:1 matches). The correct action for an occupied destination holding the SAME card is RETIRE the duplicate, not reslug onto it -- the same shape as 2026-09-21-bcp-lava-refractor-bowman-duplicate.json. This revision rewrites all 281 entries as action "retire" on the stale id alone (no "to"), re-verified by fresh point read on 2026-09-22.
rulings: CF-T206-BACK-BRAND-IS-NOT-THE-PLAYER (owner-approved 2026-09-22): the sale-side parser stuffed the T206 back-brand text into the player segment, splitting a single player across 5-8 wrong ids. Fixed in unnumberedCardSegment/hobbyIqCardId.service.ts (#2409, merged). This list is the catalog-side companion: it retires the 281 stale catalog rows minted under the year-prefixed key 1909-11-t206-baseball whose canonical t206 twin already exists.

RETIRE, NOT RESLUG -- the lesson from the refused report. relocate-catalog-rows-by-list.cjs's reslug action refuses any destination address that is already occupied. Since every canonical t206 destination in this list ALREADY holds the same player's row (that occupancy is what proved the 1:1 match), retire is the only action that lands: the stale row is deleted, the canonical row is untouched and remains the sole surviving address.

THE CANONICAL KEY IS t206, matching normalizeSetKey's own rule and the 550-row sportscardchecklist-backed checklist already stored under it (source sportscardchecklist-2026-09-05, confirmed on all 281 canonical rows by fresh point read 2026-09-22).

EVERY ENTRY WAS RE-VERIFIED BY FRESH POINT READ on 2026-09-22, after the refused report: (a) the stale row still exists, (b) the canonical row still exists with a checklist-grade source and the SAME player surname (pose carried in the canonical playerName where the checklist names one; the stale row itself never carries pose text), (c) sold_comps was checked for any sale resident at the stale id via hobbyiqCardId = id OR cardId = id. All 281 of 281 candidates passed all three checks -- ZERO have a resident sale, so none needed to be excluded and handed to the rematch separately.

THE 99 AMBIGUOUS + 41 UNMATCHED ROWS FROM THE PRIOR REVISION REMAIN EXCLUDED, unchanged: neither bucket was part of this rewrite's scope, and neither is safe to retire without the same per-row surname/pose confirmation this revision performed for the 281 -- see excluded below.

excluded.note: 99 rows whose surname matches MORE THAN ONE canonical t206 checklist row (different poses of the same player, e.g. Ty Cobb: 4 pose rows; Christy Mathewson: 4; Doc White: 2). 41 rows whose surname has ZERO matches on the 550-row canonical t206 checklist (measured against the tests/fixtures/sportscardchecklist/1909-11-t206-baseball.trimmed.html excerpt used for this PR's read-only measurement).
